subject: Priv infra CI: dependency graph, upgrade & rollback protocols
thread_summary: Review and finalize CI dependency ordering for private deployments; agree a clear, testable rollback protocol for Helm/Terraform/Ansible changes in air-gapped VPC/on-prem environments. Address artifact signing and CI gating so security can sign off.
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Patel <sam.patel@acme-analytics.com>, ops-security@acme-analytics.com
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Jun 2025 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Priv infra CI: dependency graph, upgrade & rollback protocols

Sam / Acme Ops team —

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. As we get ready to run the first end-to-end deploy in your staging VPC (air-gapped registry, signed artifacts), we need to align on two operational items before the run window this Friday:

1) CI dependency ordering across Terraform -> Helm -> Ansible (we need a deterministic graph so rollbacks are safe)
2) A minimal, testable rollback protocol that works without external internet (no public artifact fetch)

I've attached a draft dependency graph (privdeploy-dep-graph.png) and a proposed rollback-playbook.md. High level notes:
- Terraform applies networking, load balancers, and storage (object store endpoints) and must be reversible for subnet + route changes.
- Helm upgrades are the primary risk for in-cluster breakage; plan: canary namespace + pre/post hooks that validate KV cache warmup and readiness probes.
- Ansible runs node-level config (bastion keys, CA bundles, container runtime tweaks); these need idempotent checks and a safe ordering to avoid SSH lockouts.

Ask from Acme: please confirm any environment-specific constraints (image signing CA, registry mirroring cadence, and whether you require signed Helm charts or only signed OCI images).

Proposed immediate next step: 1) Acme ops confirm registry signing CA and mirror policy, 2) Red-team (ops-security) review of rollback-playbook.md, 3) We lock CI gating (merge blocker) to run the conformance pipeline against a staging cluster before any prod candidate.

Thanks,
Aditya
Principal Infra Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments: privdeploy-dep-graph.png (image/png), rollback-playbook.md (text/markdown)

From: Sam Patel <sam.patel@acme-analytics.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops-security@acme-analytics.com, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Jun 2025 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Priv infra CI: dependency graph, upgrade & rollback protocols

Aditya —

Thanks for the clear summary and the attachments. Quick answers from our side:
- Registry: we mirror images nightly from our central build cluster into the on-prem registry; images are signed with our internal JKS-backed signer (we can provide the cert bundle).
- Helm charts: we do not currently sign charts; we trust OCI image signing. If Redwood can support both signed images + chart provenance check (chartmuseum or OCI provenance), that would be ideal.
- Mirror cadence: nightly, but we can trigger ad-hoc pushes for release candidates.

We will have ops-security do a read of the rollback-playbook; initial ask: ensure the playbook never requires creating a new external NAT/GW during rollback (so no outbound internet dependence).

Sam
Platform Lead — Acme Analytics

--
ops-security@acme-analytics.com wrote:
> We will review. Two safety asks up front: (1) artifact signing verification in CI (reject unsigned), (2) a dry-run mode of rollback that can be executed against a snapshot cluster (no live changes).

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Sam Patel <sam.patel@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 01 Jul 2025 08:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Priv infra CI: dependency graph, upgrade & rollback protocols

Quick comments after skimming the dep-graph and playbook:
- Make Terraform changes non-destructive by default: add a preservation flag for subnets and PVs (terraform lifecycle ignore_changes on critical fields where appropriate). Annotate which resources require manual approval for destroy.
- Helm: adopt a two-phase upgrade job in CI: (A) dry-helm-diff + chart-verify (checks values schema + provenance), (B) canary release into a shadow namespace with automated smoke checks (KV warm, model server warm). If canary passes, promote with a gradual replica increase.
- Ansible tasks that rotate SSH keys must run from bastion with sanity-check readbacks; avoid automatic key removal — prefer staged rotation.

I've added inline notes in rollback-playbook.md (see attachment). Two blockers for security sign-off: artifact-sign verification in pipeline and a documented revert path that does not require manual DB restores.

-V
Vanessa Ortiz
Sr. Staff Engineer, Deployments
Redwood Inference

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Sam Patel <sam.patel@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 01 Jul 2025 14:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Priv infra CI: dependency graph, upgrade & rollback protocols

Adding some CI specifics and checklist items:
- Merge gating: require the following automated checks before merge into main: terraform-plan-check (no drifts that destroy subnets), chart-verify (oci signature verification), helm-diff pass, ansible-lint + idempotence test.
- Artifact handling: CI must publish signed SBOM and place artifacts in a release bucket mirrored to the air-gapped registry (we will run an in-cluster verifier job to assert signatures).
- Rollback exercise: schedule a 2-hour tabletop on Thu 10:00 with Acme ops + ops-security + Redwood infra to walk the playbook, and a dry-run in a sandbox cluster on Fri morning.

I'll create the merge-blocker GH Actions and post the PR link shortly.

-Neha
Infrastructure Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Sam Patel <sam.patel@acme-analytics.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 02 Jul 2025 16:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Priv infra CI: dependency graph, upgrade & rollback protocols

Perfect — thank you all. Short action list I will own and track:
- [A] Update dependency graph with explicit reverse-order labels for rollback steps (by EOD Thu) — aditya_rao/reference:priv-dep-graph-v2
- [B] Push GH Actions for merge gating (terraform-plan + chart-verify + helm-diff) and open PR (neha_kapoor to review) — target: Thu AM
- [C] Add artifact signature verification step to chart-verify pipeline and publish SBOMs (Jonas to handle registry verifier)
- [D] Confirm Acme CA bundle + mirror ops; ops-security to confirm no nat dependency in rollback (Sam / ops-security)
- [E] Run tabletop Thu 10:00 and sandbox dry-run Fri 09:00 (calendar invites sent)

I attached the updated playbook with Vanessa's inline comments and a flattened checklist for the run. If there are any objections to the gating sequence above, flag now — otherwise we will lock the merge window to the gating pipeline tomorrow.

Thanks,
Aditya
Principal Infra Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments: rollback-playbook.md (updated)
